Cry of the Saint
kry uv thuh saynt
noun phrase
From the Hebrew tsa‘aq and za‘aq, “to cry out, to cry for help,” and the Greek bo&aelig;, “a crying,” the loud appeal of the afflicted believer unto God.

Biblical Definition

The cry of the saint is the believer’s loud and earnest appeal unto God in his affliction, and the sure word of Scripture is that the LORD hears it. The righteous cry, and the LORD heareth, and delivereth them out of all their troubles (Psa 34:17). It is no genteel or measured thing, this cry; Heman the Ezrahite poured it out in the night season, crying day and night before God when his soul was full of troubles and his life drew nigh unto the grave (Psa 88:1-2). The Lord Jesus taught that God will avenge His own elect, which cry day and night unto Him, though He bear long with them (Luk 18:7). And under the altar the souls of the martyrs cry with a loud voice, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood (Rev 6:10). The dictionary marks that this crying is the proper voice of faith in distress, not unbelief, for the man who cries unto God still believes that God hears and will answer. The saint may cry from the depths, from the pit, from the place where no comfort comes, and yet his cry is heard in heaven and laid up before the throne. The crying of the saint is therefore a comfort and not a shame, for it leads at last to the wiping away of every tear by the hand of God Himself.

Webster 1828 Definition

The earnest appeal of the afflicted believer unto God, which the LORD surely hears.

CRY OF THE SAINT, the loud and earnest appeal of the afflicted believer unto God.

The psalmist promises that the LORD heareth the cry of the righteous.

It is poured out in the night season from the depths of trouble.

Christ taught that God avengeth His elect who cry day and night unto Him.

It witnesses to the faith that cries because it believes God hears and answers.

Key Scripture

Psa 34:17 — "The righteous cry, and the LORD heareth, and delivereth them out of all their troubles."

Psa 88:1 — "O LORD God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before thee:"

Luk 18:7 — "And shall not God avenge his own elect, which cry day and night unto him, though he bear long with them?"

Rev 6:10 — "And they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?"

Modern Corruption

A scriptural mark of true faith, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses to the LORD’s sure hearing of His afflicted people.

expand to see more

The cry of the saint is a plain and precious truth of Scripture, and no movement of the present age has set itself to redefine it. The dictionary records it that the believer who is brought low and cries from the depths may know his crying is no token of unbelief, but the proper voice of faith laying hold upon a God who hears.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the boldness of the afflicted believer at the throne of grace. He who heard Heman in the night and hears the martyrs under the altar is the same who bids His people cast their care upon Him. The saint tempted to think God deaf to his groaning may remember that the righteous cry and the LORD heareth, and that not one cry of His people falls unregarded to the ground.

Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew and Greek for “to cry out,” the cry of the saint names the believer’s appeal that God surely hears.

expand to see more

Cry of the Saint — Hebrew tsa‘aq, “to cry for help.”

The Greek bo&aelig; names “a crying” or loud appeal.

The psalmist Heman cried day and night before God in his trouble.

Christ named the elect as those who cry day and night unto Him.

The souls under the altar cry with a loud voice for the LORD’s judgment.

Usage

"Like the cry of the saint that the LORD heareth, the believer’s groaning in affliction is the proper voice of faith, not of unbelief."

"When the soul is brought to the pit, the cry that ascends from the depths is heard and laid up before the throne of God."

"The God who avengeth His own elect bids His afflicted people cry day and night, assured that He will answer in His time."
